findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on missing file, unreadable file, or I/O error
findings.failure_mode: untrusted filesystem input causes process abort instead of returning a typed error the caller can handle
findings.fix: Return Result<Vec<Record>, Error> and use .map_err(|e| Error::Io(e)) or a custom IO variant

findings.problem: parts[0] and parts[1] access without bounds check on split result of hostile input
findings.failure_mode: malformed line with fewer than 2 comma-separated fields panics via out-of-bounds index
findings.fix: Use .get(0) and .get(1).ok_or(Error::InvalidLine) or destruct with let [name, value] = parts[..] with proper error path

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on non-numeric value strings
findings.failure_mode: any non-integer value in the second CSV field causes process abort instead of returning a typed parse error
findings.fix: Use .map_err(|_| Error::ParseInt) or .ok_or(Error::InvalidValue) on the parse result

findings.problem: as u16 cast on u32 parse result silently truncates values above 65535
findings.failure_mode: a value like 70000 parses to u32 successfully then truncates to 4444 in u16 with no error, corrupting domain data
findings.fix: Use u16::try_from(parsed_u32).map_err(|_| Error::Overflow) or parse directly as u16 via .parse::<u16>()

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) embeds console I/O in domain data-loading logic
findings.failure_mode: pure domain logic leaks side effects, breaking deterministic behavior, making testing harder, and polluting stdout in library consumers
findings.fix: Remove println entirely. If logging is needed, pass a callback or log sink into the shell layer; domain code must be pure

findings.problem: No domain cap or try_reserve before collecting arbitrary CSV lines into Vec<String>
findings.failure_mode: a malicious or malformed file with millions of lines exhausts heap memory causing OOM crash
findings.fix: Validate line count against a trusted domain cap before allocation; call Vec::try_reserve(cap).map_err(|_| Error::Allocation) before the loop

findings.problem: Vec::with_capacity (via collect) allocates from untrusted input size with no checked capacity arithmetic
findings.failure_mode: overflow in total byte/count estimation could wrap to small value then panic on actual allocation, or silently under-allocate
findings.fix: Compute line count or byte budget with checked arithmetic; use try_reserve with a trusted domain cap

findings.problem: load_shards returns Vec<Record> with no error type; all failures manifest as panics via unwrap
findings.failure_mode: callers cannot distinguish IO errors, parse errors, invalid line format, or overflow — all collapse to process abort
findings.fix: Define a domain Error enum (Io, InvalidLine, ParseInt, Overflow, Allocation) and return Result<Vec<Record>, Error>

findings.problem: I/O (fs::read_to_string), parsing, logging, and domain construction are all fused in a single function
findings.failure_mode: violates Functional Core / Imperative Shell — pure domain logic cannot be unit-tested in isolation, side effects are unbounded, and the shell cannot be composed or mocked
findings.fix: Split into: (1) shell: read file, handle I/O errors; (2) parser: pure function accepting &str lines, returning Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError>; (3) domain: Record constructor with smart constructor validation

findings.problem: Record.name is a raw String with no validation or newtype protection
findings.failure_mode: empty names, embedded newlines, or null bytes are legal domain values that violate domain invariants
findings.fix: Use a Name newtype with a smart constructor that validates non-empty and clean, returning a typed error on invalid input

findings.problem: text.lines().map(...).collect() processes every line including empty or whitespace-only lines without filtering or erroring
findings.failure_mode: empty lines produce empty parts vectors that panic at parts[0] or parts[1], or whitespace-only lines create invalid Records silently
findings.fix: Filter or error on empty/blank lines before parsing; use skip_whitespace or check is_empty before split

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for load_shards throughput or latency
no allocation profiler evidence (e.g., heaptrack, valgrind massif) for memory behavior under hostile input
no command-truth evidence (cargo fmt/check/clippy/test) was run to validate the crate compiles under strict lint gates
no Miri run to verify no undefined behavior in current implementation
no proptest or property-based test for malformed CSV input behavior
no benchmark/baseline/profiler/allocation evidence for any stated performance claim
residual_risk: Static review only with no commands executed. The crate as-written will panic on any non-trivial input (missing file, empty lines, non-numeric values, values > 65535, files with fewer than 2 fields per line). All failure modes are process-abort rather than recoverable errors. Functional Core / Imperative Shell separation is entirely absent. Every Holzman absolute law is violated in this single 23-line function.
